newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply off on late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply off on late profit-taking.

text.p: A flurry of profit-taking in afternoon trade pushed Hong Kong stocks to a sharply lower close on Thursday, with a drop in HSBC Holdings Plc shares forcing the Hang Seng Index to give up some of its record ground.
The blue chip index ended 111.68 points, or 0.79 percent, lower 14,041.90 after rising to an early record high of 14,167.01 and falling to a low of 13,936.45 in late trade.
"You have had a very strong past nine days and when you have had that sort of strength it is time to take a bit of profit," said Peter Churchouse, regional strategist at Morgan Stanley.
The Hang Seng Index closed above 14,000 points for the first time on Wednesday, surging 247.12 points to 14,153.58.
"You might see a short-term breather but the liquidity, the economic fundamentals and the earnings momentum mean that this market is likely to remain strong," said Churchouse.
Turnover on Thursday was HK$16.83 billion compared with HK$17.70 billion on Wednesday.

The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said on Thursday it would upgrade its transaction capacity following a recent surge in turnover. Capacity will be raised to HK$24-28 billion this week from a current HK$20 billion and upgraded to HK$32 billion next week.
Brokers said some investors may be nervous ahead of the release later on Thursday of U.S. consumer price data.

But Churchouse said interest rate concerns should not be a major factor in the market and even if the U.S. Federal Reserve did raise interest rates at its upcoming May 20 meeting, the market should not go into a major retreat.
"Any move of 25 basis points will be probably thought to be the last we will see," Churchouse said.
Shares in HSBC Holdings led the market lower on Thursday with a drop of HK$5.00 to HK$218.00.
Red chips were also hit hard. Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd fell HK$2.00 to HK$40.20 and China Resources Enterprises Ltd dropped HK$1.35 to HK$21.50.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd gained HK$1.25 to HK$93.75 after Standard and Poor's raised its ratings on the company.
Zhejiang Expressway Co Ltd made its trading debut and ended at HK$2.50 compared with an issue price of HK$2.38.
Dragonfield Holdings Ltd also made its market debut and closed at HK$1.26 compared with an issue price of HK$1.00.
The May futures contract on the Hang Seng Index fell 230 points to 13,960 and the June contract lost 230 to 14,010.
